data.body_html:
Imagine a marbella dolphin watching picnic cruise where you glide out of Puerto Banús, the Mediterranean sun warming your skin, and within minutes you're scanning the glittering water for dorsal fins. This is the family-friendly day out that combines the thrill of spotting wild dolphins in the Alboran Sea with the relaxed pleasure of a picnic afloat. With departures from Marbella's most glamorous marina, a licensed skipper at the helm, and all drinks and snacks included, it's a stress-free way to create lasting memories. Prices start at €749 for a 2-hour charter (Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39) – no hidden costs, just you, your family, and the sea.

Why Choose a Dolphin Watching Picnic Cruise in Marbella?

Marbella's coastline is a natural highway for dolphins. The warm, nutrient-rich waters of the Alboran Sea attract common dolphins, striped dolphins, and occasionally bottlenose dolphins all year round. A dedicated dolphin watching picnic cruise gives you the best chance of an encounter because we combine the search with a leisurely cruise – no rushing, no crowds. Unlike large tourist boats, our private charters keep the group small (5–12 guests depending on the boat), so everyone gets a front-row view. Plus, you control the itinerary: spend more time near Cabopino or Cala Cortés if the dolphins are active there.

Our Family-Friendly Fleet for Dolphin Watching

We offer a range of boats from Puerto Banús, all perfectly suited for a family outing. For small families, the Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) is a stable catamaran ideal for toddlers. The Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) and Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) are our most popular Tier A choices – both offer comfortable seating, shade, and a picnic table. For larger groups, the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) and Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) provide panoramic flybridge views perfect for dolphin spotting. All boats include a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, and 21% VAT – no surprises.

What's Included in Your Picnic Cruise

Every marbella dolphin watching picnic cruise comes fully equipped for a relaxed day on the water. Your skipper handles navigation and dolphin spotting, while you enjoy:

  • Water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, and cava – unlimited throughout the charter
  • Light snacks (olives, crisps, nuts, fresh fruit)
  • Safety equipment including life jackets for all ages
  • Fuel and insurance (fully comprehensive)
  • Spanish IVA (21%) included in the price

You are welcome to bring your own picnic or a birthday cake – just avoid glass bottles for safety. The crew will provide plates, glasses, and ice.

Best Times and Spots for Dolphin Sightings

Dolphins are most active in the early morning (9am–11am) and late afternoon (4pm–6pm) when the sea is calmest. Our skippers head towards the Cabopino area (about 3 nautical miles from Puerto Banús) and the Cala del Faro region, where baitfish congregate and dolphins follow. In summer, the Estepona coastline also yields frequent sightings. A 2-hour charter covers roughly 10–15 nautical miles; a 4-hour charter (€1,299) extends to the Marbella Marina or even Sotogrande. For the best odds, book a half-day or full-day trip.

Pricing and Booking Your Dolphin Watching Picnic Cruise

Our Tier A boats – Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39 – are priced at €749 for 2 hours, €1,299 for 4 hours, and €2,299 for 8 hours. This includes everything: skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and VAT. For larger boats like the Mangusta 80, pricing starts at €4,719 for a minimum 4-hour charter (includes a free jet ski). All other boats are priced on request via WhatsApp. To book, simply [contact us](/experiences/marbella-dolphin-watching-picnic-cruise/) or send a WhatsApp message. We recommend booking 48 hours ahead, especially in peak summer (July–August).

What to Bring and Wear

Pack light: swimwear, a towel, sun cream (SPF 50+), sunglasses with a strap, and a light jacket or windbreaker – even in summer, the sea breeze can be cool. A hat is essential. Cameras and phones are fine, but a waterproof case is smart. Children should wear a life jacket (provided) when on deck. No high heels on the boat – barefoot or soft-soled shoes are best.
